In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed opportunistic hyperchannels with the minSrcRR protocol provide a practical solution to the QoS assurance in light-trail networks.
the proposed opportunistic hyperchannel and minSrcRR protocol are promising to be a good candidate to carry QoS sensitive IP traffic over optical networks.
the proposed minSrcRR protocol can achieve a better performance in terms of throughput and delay than the conventional light-trail protocol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
opportunistic hyperchannels can be used to carry IP traffic with QoS guarantee over optical networks.

the proposed opportunistic hyperchannel architecture is able to support QoS guarantee in a fully distributed manner and the proposed minSrcRR protocol can effectively assure QoS in an opportunistic hyper-channel.
the proposed opportunistic hyperchannel architecture and minSrcRR protocol can be a good choice in the next generation IP optical networks to provide QoS guarantee and high-speed provisioning.

opportunistic hyperchannels can provide an alternative way to implement QoS-assuring light-trails.
opportunistic hyperchannels provide a promising solution to carry IP traffic in future high-capacity optical transport networks.
